title: Search the tree: rg, pipes, and jq
tagline: Find the string, shape the JSON, don't drown in output
interviewPrompt: You need to find every call site for a broken API route and confirm the JSON shape. Walk me through it on the command line.

beats.interviewer: You're in a big monorepo. Find every reference to /api/phone-cam without opening the IDE search UI.
beats.interviewee: From the repo root: rg -n "phone-cam" --glob '!node_modules'. rg is ripgrep — recursive, respects gitignore, fast enough to feel instant.

beats.interviewer: You got three thousand hits. Now what? How do you not drown?
beats.interviewee: Narrow: rg -n "phone-cam" -g '*.ts' -g '!**/dist/**' app components. Then pipe a JSON dump if the tool emits JSON: … | jq '.[] | .path'.
beats.show: Filter globs, then jq for structure.

beats.interviewer: What breaks first for juniors here?
beats.interviewee: Piping binary garbage into jq, or forgetting quotes so the shell eats the pattern. And running from the wrong cwd so rg 'finds nothing' that exists two levels up.
beats.show: break: bad cwd, unquoted pattern, jq on non-JSON.

beats.interviewer: Show me a safe daily habit.
beats.interviewee: pwd first. Then rg with a tight glob. Prefer | head while exploring. Commit only after git diff shows the intentional change — search is read-only; edit is a separate step.
beats.show: pwd → tight rg → head → intentional edit.
